subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory CRUD write contract to memory-core, and if so what hard-limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it would create a new public memory-write API plus security, persistence, and config behavior that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
options.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, and secret policy before code lands.

options.title: Narrow to existing paths
options.body: Keep first-class CRUD out of core for now and address bloat through the existing memory-flush, promotion, and recall surfaces.

options.title: Prototype externally first
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype the write policy as a memory plugin or ClawHub package until a core or plugin API gap is proven.

recommendation.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
recommendation.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, and secret policy before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing signal is recent memory-core and plugin-boundary ownership around the recall-only tool surface and persistence behavior.
